include.description: More config files to read first, by path or pattern. What this file says wins.

default-profile.description: The profile new tabs open with, by id.

profile-order.description: Profile ids in the order the menus list them.

keys.description: Key bindings: a chord or sequence ("ctrl+shift+t", "ctrl+a > c") and the action it runs, or "none".

family.title: Font
family.description: Any monospace font. Nerd Fonts also show prompt icons.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: How heavy normal text is. A font without that weight shows its nearest one.

ligatures.title: Ligatures
ligatures.description: Fonts that have them (Cascadia Code, JetBrains Mono, Fira Code) join => != -> and the like into one shape. Each character keeps its own cell, and the character under the cursor isn't joined.

fallback.title: Fallback fonts
fallback.description: For characters your font lacks, tried in order before Windows picks one. Separate them with commas.

adjust-cell-height.title: Line height
adjust-cell-height.description: More room between lines, as a percentage (20%) or in pixels (2). A negative value gives less. Text stays centered.

builtin-glyphs.title: Built-in glyphs
builtin-glyphs.description: Zinc draws box lines, blocks and Powerline shapes itself, so they join up in any font.

adjust-box-thickness.title: Line thickness
adjust-box-thickness.description: Thicker or thinner built-in lines, in pixels (1, -1) or as a percentage (20%).

theme.title: Color scheme
theme.description: About 650 are included. Add your own to the themes folder next to config.toml.

palette-generate.title: Match 256 colors to the scheme
palette-generate.description: Programs that use the extended 256 colors (vim and htop themes) get shades made from the scheme's 16, not the standard ones.

palette-harmonious.title: Shades from background to text in light schemes
palette-harmonious.description: When off, shades run from dark to light, which is what programs expect.

cursor-text.title: Cursor text
cursor-text.description: The character under a block cursor. If the scheme doesn't set one either, it's the background color.

selection-background.title: Selection
selection-background.description: Behind selected text. If the scheme doesn't set one either, selection inverts the colors.

selection-foreground.title: Selected text
selection-foreground.description: If the scheme doesn't set one either, the text keeps its color, or inverts with the selection when "Selection" has no color either.

pane-header.title: Pane headers
pane-header.description: Behind pane titles and tabs. On cards, the border is a step stronger.

minimum-contrast.title: Minimum contrast
minimum-contrast.description: Text that reads poorly against its background turns black or white. 1 turns it off, 4.5 is the usual accessibility level, and 21 makes all text black or white.

bold-is-bright.title: Bold in bright colors
bold-is-bright.description: Bold text in the first eight colors shows their bright versions, as older terminals did.

bold.title: Bold text color
bold.description: For bold text in the default text color.

faint-opacity.title: Faint text
faint-opacity.description: How bright dim text is (1: as bright as other text).

find-highlight-current.title: Current match
find-highlight-current.description: Behind the match Find is on.

cursor-opacity.title: Cursor opacity
cursor-opacity.description: 1: solid. Lower lets the character under a block cursor show in its own color.

background-opacity.title: Terminal background opacity
background-opacity.description: Lower lets the window background show behind the text (1: solid). Colored cells stay solid.

palette.description: Palette colors by number (palette.1 = "#AC4242") are set in config.toml.

cursor-style.title: Cursor shape
cursor-style.description: Until a program picks its own (vim's insert mode often does).

cursor-style-at-prompt.title: Cursor at the prompt
cursor-style-at-prompt.description: While the shell waits for a command. A program's own cursor still wins. Needs shell integration.

padding-x.title: Padding left and right
padding-x.description: Between the window's edge and the text.

padding-y.title: Padding top and bottom
padding-y.description: Between the window's edge and the text.

padding-balance.title: Even padding
padding-balance.description: Splits the leftover space between both sides. When off, all of it goes to the right and bottom.

shell-integration.title: Shell integration
shell-integration.description: Marks prompts and commands in PowerShell, bash and zsh (WSL too), so you can jump between prompts, copy a command's output and see which commands failed.

command-marks.title: Command marks
command-marks.description: The bar beside a command's output.

reload-environment.title: Pick up environment changes
reload-environment.description: New tabs read PATH and other variables from Windows as they start, so an installer's changes work without restarting Zinc.

program-titles.title: Program titles
program-titles.description: Shells and programs set the tab's title (often the folder or the running command). When off, tabs show the profile's name.

shell-titles.title: Folder and command as the title
shell-titles.description: The folder at the prompt, the running command otherwise. A program's own title still wins. Needs shell integration.

scrollback-lines.title: Scrollback lines
scrollback-lines.description: How far back you can scroll.

word-boundaries.title: Word boundaries
word-boundaries.description: Characters that end a word when you double-click (space and tab always do). Empty: the ones shown.

click-to-move.title: Click to move the cursor
click-to-move.description: At a shell prompt, clicking in the command you're typing moves the cursor there. Needs shell integration.

right-click.title: Right-click
right-click.description: Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens the menu anywhere.

link-click.title: Open links with
link-click.description: Web links and files shown in the terminal.

middle-click-paste.title: Middle-click pastes
middle-click-paste.description: Unless the program uses the mouse.

copy-on-select.title: Copy on select
copy-on-select.description: Copies text as soon as you select it. The selection stays.

copy-formatting.title: Copy with formatting
copy-formatting.description: Copies colors and styles too, for documents and email. Apps that take plain text still get plain text.

paste-warning.title: Paste warning
paste-warning.description: Ask before pasting text with more than one line.

large-paste-warning.title: Large pastes
large-paste-warning.description: Ask before pasting more than 5 KB.

clipboard-write.title: Programs may copy
clipboard-write.description: Copying with OSC 52, as tmux, neovim and remote shells do.

clipboard-read.title: Programs reading the clipboard
clipboard-read.description: Anything running, including a remote host, could read it.

bell.title: Bell
bell.description: When a program rings it, e.g. at a failed tab completion.

screen-flash-bell.title: Visual bell
screen-flash-bell.description: Programs that flash the screen instead of beeping (Git Bash does) ring Zinc's bell, as set in "Bell".

input-method.title: Input methods
input-method.description: Type Japanese, Chinese, Korean and more with Windows' input methods (IME). Turn it off if keys behave oddly.

appearance.title: Light or dark
appearance.description: Windows, menus and dialogs. The terminal keeps its color scheme. Restart Zinc to apply.

accent.title: Accent color
accent.description: Selections, focus lines, switches and buttons. Restart Zinc to apply.

backdrop.title: Window background
backdrop.description: What's behind everything in the window: tabs, sidebar and terminal.

backdrop-tint.title: Window tint
backdrop-tint.description: How much color an acrylic or clear background carries. Lower is more see-through.

backdrop-color.title: Window tint color
backdrop-color.description: The color an acrylic or clear background is tinted with.

workspace-tabs.title: Workspaces
workspace-tabs.description: Tabs along the top, or a list in a sidebar. Applies to windows opened from now on.

new-workspace-page.title: Start page for new workspaces
new-workspace-page.description: Choose a profile, a folder and a name when you open a workspace. Enter starts the default profile.

workspace-colors.title: Colors for new workspaces
workspace-colors.description: For the ones you don't color yourself.

start-in.title: New tabs and splits start
start-in.description: New tabs in a workspace with its own folder start there. Without "Tabs inside panes", this is for splits only, because a new tab is a new workspace.

pane-tabs.title: Tabs inside panes
pane-tabs.description: Each pane can hold several tabs.

pane-headers.title: Pane headers
pane-headers.description: The row above a pane. Its tabs, or its title when it has one tab.

pane-header-buttons.title: Header buttons
pane-header-buttons.description: Split, maximize and more on the right of a pane's header, with a program's progress beside them.

pane-gap.title: Gap between panes
pane-gap.description: Above 0, panes are rounded cards with space between them. At 0 they meet at a thin divider.

pane-gap-edges.title: Gap at the workspace edges
pane-gap-edges.description: The same gap around the outside, split or not, so splitting never moves a pane's outer edges. Only with a "Gap between panes" above 0.

pane-focus.title: Show focus with
pane-focus.description: How the focused pane stands out from the others.

pane-animations.title: Pane animations
pane-animations.description: Panes slide into place when you split, close, maximize or move them. They don't while "Animation effects" is off in Windows Settings.

pane-resize-step.title: Resize step
pane-resize-step.description: How far a resize key moves the divider, as a share of the panes it splits.

unfocused-pane-opacity.title: Unfocused panes
unfocused-pane-opacity.description: How bright unfocused panes stay (1: not dimmed).

divider-color.title: Divider color
divider-color.description: The line between split panes, when "Gap between panes" is 0.

save-state.title: Reopen windows
save-state.description: Windows, workspaces, splits and tabs come back in their folders.

launch-at-login.title: When you sign in to Windows

explorer-menu.title: Open in Zinc from File Explorer
explorer-menu.description: Adds "Open in Zinc" to the right-click menu of folders and drives. On Windows 11 it's under "Show more options".

confirm-close.title: Ask before closing
confirm-close.description: When a tab, pane, workspace or window you close still runs a command, or holds two or more tabs. Zinc knows a command is running through shell integration.

confirm-quit.title: Ask before quitting with a running command
confirm-quit.description: When you quit Zinc (or restart it for an update) while a command still runs.

focus-follows-mouse.title: Focus follows mouse
focus-follows-mouse.description: Moving the pointer into a pane focuses it.

low-latency-drawing.title: Low-latency drawing
low-latency-drawing.description: What you type shows up about one screen refresh sooner. Turn it off if a terminal draws wrong or stops drawing, and tell us. Applies to terminals opened from now on.

free-hidden-memory.title: Free memory of hidden tabs
free-hidden-memory.description: Background tabs, minimized windows and the dismissed quick terminal give back their graphics memory and rebuild it when you return. Turn it off if switching tabs flashes. Only with "Low-latency drawing".

software-rendering.title: Software rendering
software-rendering.description: Draws with the processor instead of the graphics card, which is slower. Use it for broken graphics drivers, some virtual machines and remote desktop glitches. Applies to terminals opened from now on.

tab-groups.description: An old name for pane-tabs. It still works.

pane-tab-strip.description: An old name for pane-headers. It still works.

group-tab-strip.description: An old name for pane-headers. It still works.

unfocused-split-opacity.description: An old name for unfocused-pane-opacity. It still works.

unfocused-split-fill.description: An old name for unfocused-pane-fill. It still works.

files.title: Custom shaders
files.description: Effects drawn over the terminal, such as CRT screens, glow and cursor trails. They're GLSL files written for Ghostty or Shadertoy, and they run in order.

animation.title: Animation
animation.description: For animated shaders. The others redraw only when the terminal changes.

folders.description: Folders of shaders to choose from. Add and remove them on the shaders page (the library's … menu).

remote-control.title: Remote control
remote-control.description: Lets zn, Zinc's command-line tool, open, arrange and close tabs, type into them and read them. Any program running as you could use it.

path.title: Use zn in other terminals
path.description: Adds zn to your PATH, so other terminals find it too (Zinc's own terminals always do). Shells started from now on see it.

command-finished.title: Long command finishes
command-finished.description: In a pane you weren't looking at.

command-finished-sound.title: Sound
command-finished-sound.description: Plays when a long command finishes out of view (a Windows notification has its own).

programs.title: Program notifications
programs.description: When a program asks for one, e.g. a build script finishing (OSC 9 or 777).

finished-color.title: Finished
finished-color.description: A command finished, or a program sent a notification.

failed-color.title: Failed
failed-color.description: A command failed, or a program exited with an error.

hotkey.title: Hotkey
hotkey.description: Shows and hides the quick terminal from anywhere, e.g. win+grave or ctrl+alt+t.

size.title: Size
size.description: A percentage or pixels (50%, 600px) along its edge. Empty: 50%, or 70% by 60% at "Center".

animation-duration.title: Animation
animation-duration.description: How long the quick terminal takes to fade in and out. At 0 it appears at once.

check.title: Check for updates automatically
check.description: Once a day. New versions download in the background, and you choose when to restart. Only for Zinc installed with its installer.

logging.title: Debug log
logging.description: Keeps a record of what Zinc does, to send with a bug report. Turn it on, make the problem happen, then copy the log.

environment.description: Environment variables for the programs Zinc starts. An empty value removes one.

command.title: Command
command.description: What runs in its tabs: a shell, or any program.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: An image file for its tabs (default: the program's own icon).

hidden.title: Hidden
hidden.description: Kept out of the menus (its tabs still reopen).

profile.description: A profile: a shell or program, and settings of its own.
